label: copy-phase input of the letter a (from the 3rd copy step on)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, on steps where the token fed back in is the letter a (a fed back copy of an original a). It is silent during the original phase and on the <DEL> step, even when the input is a, and it is silent on every other input token. It almost never fires at recall_idx 1, where the input is orig(0). About 79% of copy-phase a inputs activate it, and the misses are weak. Magnitude is highest when a is followed by another a in the original (an aa pair), where the first a of the pair gets close to the max activation. It is also larger at mid-to-late copy positions. Isolated a inputs give weaker activations.

issues: The core claims hold. All activation mass is in the copy phase (original 0, delimiter 0). in_tok=a holds 100% of mass. At recall_idx 1 the feature is almost silent (precision 0.006 over 16,744 a inputs). Top activations are on the first a of an aa pair (out_tok==a: precision 0.994). Test scores reproduce: P 0.792, R 0.999, F1 0.884, mass recall 0.9996.

The 21% of false positives are systematic, not scattered noise. By recall_idx, dev precision is 0.545 at recall_idx 2, then 0.897 at 3, 0.928 at 4 and 0.818 at 5 and above. Including recall_idx 2 in the predicate (the 'from the 3rd copy step on' wording) treats a coin-flip position as part of the feature.

Whether the feature fires also depends on the neighbouring original tokens, and the explanation does not mention this. By prev_tok, precision ranges from 0.51 (c) and 0.54 (digit 0) to 0.95 (g, q). By out_tok (the token after a in the original), it ranges from 0.39 (digit 2), 0.56 (h, z) and 0.60 (e) to 0.98-0.99 (a, f, r). For example, out_tok in DIGITS gives precision 0.682 and prev_tok in DIGITS gives 0.735.
Precision is also lower for short sequences (L<=4: 0.659) and for a inputs with many outputs left (to_go>=6: 0.589). This fits a graded magnitude that only crosses threshold later in the copy phase.
Dropping recall_idx 2 entirely is not a fix: test P 0.867, R 0.849, F1 0.858. Recall_idx 2 carries about 10% of the mass, so the fix has to be conditional on the neighbouring tokens.
skeptic.revised_label: copy-phase input of the letter a (recall_idx >= 2), weakened at recall_idx 2 and by certain neighbouring original tokens (e.g. preceded by c or a digit, followed by a digit, h or z)

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token (most: a, -, r, c, g, s; least: m, u, v, 0) and the token being output (most: a, f, r, p, b, y; least: e, h, 2, -); timing cues that raise it most: recall_idx=4, recall_idx=3, L=5 & t=8.
